draft.title: Features of a parabola
card: Vertex
the turning point of the parabola, its highest or lowest point. It is the lowest point when the parabola is concave up and the highest when it is concave down.
Axis of symmetry
the vertical line through the vertex. It splits the parabola into two mirror halves. In a table, equal y-values sit the same distance either side of it.
Intercepts
the y-intercept is where the curve crosses the y-axis, at \(x = 0\). The x-intercepts are where it crosses the x-axis, at \(y = 0\). There can be two, one or none.
Example
For \(y = x^{2} - 4\), the vertex is \((0, -4)\), the axis of symmetry is \(x = 0\), the y-intercept is \(-4\), and the x-intercepts are \(x = -2\) and \(x = 2\).

4.alt: The parabola \(y = x^{2} - 4\), concave up, with vertex \((0, -4)\), crossing the x-axis at \(x = -2\) and \(x = 2\) and the y-axis at \(-4\).

draft.remember: The vertex is the turning point, the axis of symmetry runs through it, and the intercepts are where the curve meets the axes.

a.q: A parabola has a table of values with \(y = 5\) at both \(x = 1\) and \(x = 5\). Which line is its axis of symmetry?
a.why: Equal y-values sit the same distance either side of the axis, so the axis is halfway between \(x = 1\) and \(x = 5\), at \(x = 3\). The line \(y = 5\) is horizontal, but the axis of symmetry is vertical.
a.clue: The axis is halfway between the two x-values.

b.q: Mia's parabola is \(y = 9 - x^{2}\). It is concave down. What are its vertex and y-intercept?
b.why: At \(x = 0\), \(y = 9 - 0 = 9\). This is the y-intercept, and it is also the highest point, so it is the vertex \((0, 9)\). The value 3 is an x-intercept, found where \(y = 0\), not the y-intercept.
